artifacts.summary: Larger runners are unavailable to this personal free-plan account; forking docgen-action is unnecessary; the real OOM lever is the LEAN_NUM_THREADS env var (caps Lean's Task thread pool that Lake's job scheduler runs on), confirmed by Lake/Lean maintainers, leanprover/lean-action's own README for the identical leanchecker-OOM case, and opencompl/veir's production docs.yml fixing this exact doc-gen4 OOM. Recommends setting LEAN_NUM_THREADS: "1" on the docgen-action step in docs.yml.

memory_candidates.content: When a Mathlib-dependent Lean project's CI OOMs during a parallel Lake-driven build (lake build, doc-gen4, leanchecker/lean4checker) on a GitHub-hosted runner, the fix is NOT a Lake -j/--jobs flag (Lake 5.0 has none, because Lean gives host programs no API to cap its own Task thread pool). The actual knob is the LEAN_NUM_THREADS environment variable, read once at Lean-runtime startup, which directly caps that thread pool and therefore Lake's effective build concurrency. Unset, it defaults to the machine's hardware concurrency (e.g. 4 on a standard public-repo GitHub ubuntu-latest runner). Confirmed by Lake/Lean maintainers on the leanprover-community Zulip, documented authoritatively in leanprover/lean-action's README ('Run leanchecker on a project with a Mathlib dependency', recommending LEAN_NUM_THREADS: "1"), and used in production by opencompl/veir's docs.yml specifically to stop a doc-gen4 build OOMing ('Lake runs one job per core... run out of memory'). Set it as a step- or job-level env var in the workflow YAML; it reaches the underlying lake build subprocess by ordinary environment inheritance, no action-level input or fork required.

GitHub larger hosted runners are unavailable to a personal/user-owned repository at any billing plan tier -- the feature is documented as limited to organizations and enterprises on GitHub Team/Enterprise Cloud plans. Repository visibility (public vs private) does not change this; public repos only get free/unlimited STANDARD runner minutes, never access to larger runner sizes. Before recommending a larger-runner fix for any CI resource problem, first confirm via `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>` and `gh api user` whether the repo is org-owned, since this route is categorically closed for a personal account regardless of preference or payment.
